Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Position-aware normal-bank pseudo-masks: matching each patch only to normal patches from the same anatomical neighbourhood
SUMMARY: Keep normal-bank pseudo-masks from image labels but substitute global nearest-neighbour search with a neighbourhood-restricted search over normal patches at the same grid position (+/- 2 patches), so anatomy that is normal elsewhere cannot hide an anomaly.
HYPOTHESIS: Position-aware matching raises pseudo-mask IoU by at least 0.08 over global kNN on BrainMRI and LiverCT training images (roughly spatially aligned) without reducing it on RESC, and the resulting segmentation adapters gain at least 2 held-out PRO points over global-kNN pseudo-masks.
RATIONALE: The parent's reviewed weakness is that global nearest-neighbour distances may fail for subtle medical anomalies: a lesion patch can resemble normal tissue from a different location (e.g. a hyperintense lesion resembling normal ventricles or skull), giving a small distance and a missed pseudo-mask. Brain MRI slices in BMAD come from co-registered volumes and liver CT slices are roughly centred, so restricting matches to the same spatial neighbourhood is a better normality model. The substitution keeps the parent's framing (image labels define normality, pseudo-masks supervise the segmentation branch) and its evaluation.
METHOD: 1) For each source dataset, store normal patch tokens per grid position (17x17) and level, coreset 20% per position. 2) For a patch at (u, v) of an abnormal image, distance = 1 - max cosine over bank tokens at positions within +/-2 in u and v. 3) Pseudo-mask = patches above the 99th percentile of the same score on held-out normal images of that dataset, foreground-restricted. 4) Datasets without spatial alignment (OCT17, ChestXray, HIS): a neighbourhood radius selected per dataset on its normal images (largest radius at which normal-vs-normal false positives stay below 1%). 5) Train segmentation adapters with Focal + Dice; code: make_bank_masks.py with position index.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: global kNN pseudo-masks (parent); mask-supervised MVFA; asymmetric MIL. Ablations: radius 0/1/2/4; coreset ratio. Metrics: pseudo-mask IoU per dataset (analysis), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: no IoU gain on BrainMRI and LiverCT.

Idea B:
TITLE: Equivariance-regularised MIL: geometric consistency as free supervision for mask-free segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Add to asymmetric MIL a self-supervised constraint that the segmentation map of a geometrically transformed image equals the transformed map of the original, which pushes MIL's sparse, most-discriminative activations to cover whole lesions.
HYPOTHESIS: Adding an equivariance consistency loss to asymmetric SigLIP-MIL increases held-out PRO by at least 2 points and pixel AUROC by at least 1 point, with image AUROC unchanged within 1 point.
RATIONALE: By analogy with self-supervised equivariant attention in weakly supervised semantic segmentation (SEAM), image-level supervision yields maps that depend on arbitrary details of a single view and cover only the most discriminative parts; demanding equivariance under rescaling and flips is a free, label-independent signal that regularises maps towards object extent. Here it acts on MVFA's segmentation-branch maps at all four levels and uses only the images already in training.
METHOD: 1) For each training image x, sample a transform A (rescale 0.75-1.0 then pad, horizontal flip with p 0.5). 2) Maps M(x), M(A x) per level; consistency loss L_eq = || A(M(x)) - M(A x) ||_1 averaged over pixels and levels, weight 0.5. 3) Total loss = asymmetric SigLIP-MIL + L_eq. 4) Doubles the forward passes per step (feasible: adapters are small, backbone frozen). 5) Code: train_zero.py augmentation pair; loss.py equivariance_loss().
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: asymmetric MIL; graph-Laplacian MIL; mask-supervised MVFA. Ablations: transforms; weight; levels. Metrics: held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: PRO gain below 1 point.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
